Blind dispatch resolves identity inside the gateway

nodes.label: AegisFlow synthetic portfolio demonstration
nodes.rationale: Engineering demonstration of encrypted intake, Gemini routing, clinician approval, onboarding and CRM synchronization. It is not a clinical service or a HIPAA-certified system.

nodes.label: Next.js security gateway
nodes.rationale: Deterministic application boundary owns encryption, authenticated tools, signed callbacks, CRM integration and actual notification delivery. Workflow orchestration is split from these sensitive responsibilities.

nodes.label: Patient intake portal
nodes.rationale: Synthetic presets make ordinary and emergency paths reproducible. Same-browser identical submissions are deliberately deduplicated; change the synthetic email for a fresh case.

nodes.label: Patient Vault
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL retains encrypted identity, raw symptoms and onboarding data. Decryption keys stay in the Next.js server boundary; scrubbed text still requires caution.

nodes.label: Consent records
nodes.rationale: Consent and audit records commit transactionally with the intake and outbox. The consent text and identity checks are demonstrations, not legally validated workflows.

nodes.label: Append-only AuditLog
nodes.rationale: A PostgreSQL BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger rejects mutation. State transitions and clinician decryption views create attributed append-only records.

nodes.label: Durable leased OutboxDelivery
nodes.rationale: An encrypted dispatch payload commits with intake. Leases prevent simultaneous claims and allow crashed workers to recover; delivery is at-least-once.

nodes.label: Two-layer idempotency
nodes.rationale: Submission/browser-scoped unique keys reduce duplicate intake. Full-UUID CRM aliases and a unique deal UUID support retry-safe upserts; token row locks serialize booking.

nodes.label: Contextual and six-pass scrubber
nodes.rationale: Known form entities supplement regex because names are hard to identify with regex alone. Avoids an additional NLP service; unknown third-party identifiers can survive and arbitrary de-identification is not guaranteed.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM field encryption
nodes.rationale: Native crypto uses a fresh 12-byte IV and 16-byte authentication tag in v1:iv:authTag:ciphertext format. Authentication detects ciphertext tampering.

nodes.label: Timestamp-bound HMAC webhooks
nodes.rationale: HMAC-SHA256 authenticates timestamp plus raw body in both directions. Timing-safe comparison and a plus/minus 300-second acceptance window reduce spoofing and replay exposure.

nodes.label: Browser-scoped X-Ray inspector
nodes.rationale: UI reveals ciphertext, redaction, dispatch and CRM progress while excluding raw redaction originals and capabilities from telemetry. It distinguishes live, simulated, and preview states.

nodes.label: Clinician human review
nodes.rationale: The clinician reviews decrypted synthetic intake and the AI suggestion before approval generates the invitation. Critical cases cannot be approved.

nodes.label: One-click clinician JWT
nodes.rationale: A real one-hour jose JWT with CLINICIAN role and dr_chen_demo actor removes recruiter signup friction. This demo identity is intentionally restricted to synthetic data and does not replace a staff identity provider.

nodes.label: Single-use 48-hour onboarding capability
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 is the permanent lookup key. A user-approved temporary AES-GCM encrypted original supports delayed Gmail delivery and is cleared after confirmed send, expiry, or booking; plaintext never goes to n8n or telemetry.

nodes.label: Atomic onboarding and token burn
nodes.rationale: A database row lock serializes capability consumption so concurrent submissions cannot book twice. Used links show a receipt; completion replay is rejected.

nodes.label: Pseudonymous full-UUID CRM alias
nodes.rationale: The user-approved alias is patient_uuid@vault.example.com with Patient_short_uuid. HubSpot rejected the old internal domain; full UUID avoids contact-upsert collisions. Aliases are never email recipients.

nodes.label: HubSpot contacts and deal pipeline
nodes.rationale: Real external CRM uses pseudonymous contacts and a unique patient UUID deal property. Intake, approval and completed booking advance a dedicated pipeline without direct patient identity.

nodes.label: Application CRM gateway
nodes.rationale: README architecture routes pseudonymous contact/deal writes from the Next.js gateway to HubSpot; orchestration requests the lifecycle transition. PRD native HubSpot node descriptions are specification-level blueprints.

nodes.label: Workflow 1: Gemini triage
nodes.rationale: Original workflow ID TCc5M9TUgKMpOJHN runs a published triage webhook on the selected 5678 instance. It invokes tools, returns validated triage, and orchestrates initial CRM synchronization.

nodes.label: Workflow 2: approval and blind dispatch
nodes.rationale: Published workflow AegisOnboardingDispatch02 handles approval-stage CRM progression and signed blind notification requests; no raw invitation or actual email is sent to n8n.

nodes.label: Workflow 3: appointment completion
nodes.rationale: Published workflow AegisOnboardingComplete03 advances CRM after booking. Booking completion is durable locally while the background synchronization recovers independently.

nodes.label: Workflow 4: sanitized error handler
nodes.rationale: AegisErrorDlq04 is an Error Trigger reference rather than a webhook. Documentation describes global failure callbacks and explicit triage failure callbacks; presence of the export alone is not proof that every runtime workflow error is connected.

nodes.label: Gemini tool-calling agent
nodes.rationale: Verified Oct16 configuration used models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite. The agent invokes tools and emits structured routing advice; a routing recommendation is not a diagnosis.

nodes.label: Synthetic insurance HTTP tool
nodes.rationale: An authenticated HTTP endpoint supplies illustrative payer eligibility and copay values. It does not verify actual payer coverage.

nodes.label: Synthetic routing-rules HTTP tool
nodes.rationale: An authenticated HTTP endpoint supplies specialty routing rules and emergency criteria as model tool context.

nodes.label: XML delimiters and dual JSON validation
nodes.rationale: Untrusted symptom text is isolated with XML-style delimiters; an n8n structured output parser and Next.js Zod schema validate output shape. These are mitigations and do not prove semantic correctness or injection immunity.
nodes.norm_label: xml delimiters and dual json validation

nodes.label: CRITICAL emergency short-circuit
nodes.rationale: A critical routing result displays an emergency advisory and blocks approval on the server. PRD Slack/Discord alert expectations are not established as implemented by current README verification.

nodes.label: Blind notification endpoint
nodes.rationale: n8n submits a signed patient UUID. Next.js resolves the real address and capability inside the vault boundary and calls the actual email provider, keeping both out of workflow payloads.

nodes.label: Gmail OAuth delivery
nodes.rationale: The app refreshes Gmail access from its environment and performs sent-mail search. A stable subject reference reduces duplicate sending after ambiguous timeouts because Gmail rewrote the custom Message-ID; external exactly-once delivery is not guaranteed.

nodes.label: PREVIEW_ONLY notification mode
nodes.rationale: The documented manual-test configuration displays the invitation on screen and sends no email. A controlled test inbox must be explicitly configured for actual Gmail delivery.

nodes.label: Explicit offline simulation
nodes.rationale: Simulation requires demo mode plus DEMO_SIMULATE_N8N_IF_SLEEPING=true. The Oct16 verified live configuration left fallback disabled; simulated execution is visibly labeled and must not produce fake live CRM identifiers.

nodes.label: Timeout, retry and callback reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Three-second HTTP timeout, bounded exponential retry and a two-minute missing-callback check return unfinished work to the queue. Five unsuccessful attempts fail the delivery; authenticated manual retry can requeue triage.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 persistent database
nodes.rationale: The database uses a named volume and a loopback 5434 host mapping to container 5432. Persistent state, consent, audit, idempotency and outbox survive application restarts.

nodes.label: Selected existing n8n on 5678
nodes.rationale: This machine uses the original instance and the same four workflow IDs. Docker app reaches host.docker.internal:5678; n8n calls host.docker.internal:3005. Unrelated workflows and saved credential storage are preserved.

nodes.label: Optional isolated n8n on 5679
nodes.rationale: Fresh compose installs create a dedicated n8n 2.29.10 with a persistent named volume. README/runbook state this alternative was stopped after moving the app to the selected 5678 instance.

nodes.label: Local Docker app on 3005
nodes.rationale: Next.js standalone app maps loopback 3005 to container 3000. Compose migration profile runs prisma migrate deploy, and the configured public origin permits the intended browser origin through port mapping. Public hosting was deferred.

nodes.label: Historical Oct16 verification evidence
nodes.rationale: Recorded results: 11 unit/security, 12 PostgreSQL integration and six browser scenarios; one authorized Gmail self-test and four illustrative AI cases. These are historical checks, not fresh runtime health proof or clinical validation.

nodes.label: Portfolio limits and remaining work
nodes.rationale: Real patient use requires staff identity, clinical evaluation, provider agreements and retention review, operational/key management, monitoring, backups and abuse controls. Progress still lists blocked deletion of four local credential exports; upstream dependency advisories remain documented.

nodes.label: Modern shared frontend and journey rail
nodes.rationale: Shared components and scoped af CSS unify intake, review and onboarding. A four-stage journey rail makes the process legible; technical evidence stays behind disclosures. Local Sora/Manrope fonts, keyboard focus, reduced motion and mobile checks support the experience.
nodes.norm_label: modern shared frontend and journey rail
